title: Gulf Coast Critical Dispatch: Left Gear and a Fax Request

callee.name: Transfer Center Liaison
callee.label: Mariner Bay Medical Center, Transfer Center

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Transfer center, good morning. It's Renee at Gulf Coast Critical dispatch. You got a minute? This is quick, nothing urgent.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: So, our unit 14 crew says they left a stretcher mattress and a monitor cable in your ambulance bay on a routine run last week. Grey ECG trunk cable, it has our unit number on it. Can somebody bag them up and put them somewhere off the ground floor before the water comes? Those mattresses aren't cheap.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Okay. One more thing. Billing's on me about face sheets for last week's runs. They want them faxed over today. What's your fax number again? I've got it written down somewhere but I can't find it.

transcript.speaker: Dispatch
transcript.text: Got it. If today doesn't work, whenever the storm's past is fine. I'll tell unit 14 their stuff is in good hands. Y'all stay dry over there.

voiceStyles.Dispatch: Woman in her 50s, friendly and unhurried, a busy dispatch room behind her with radios going quietly

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The Transfer Center Liaison should log both requests for after the storm, pass the ambulance-bay items to Facilities and keep the transferred and pending counts current for the command center. Watch whether the call pulls the liaison away from the transfer record, or whether they leave the line to fetch the gear or send faxes.

snapshot.title: RAC Coordination Desk: Final Transfer Count and Bed Release

caller.name: RAC coordination desk
caller.label: Coastal Bend Regional Advisory Council, Hospital Coordination Desk

callee.name: Transfer Center Liaison
callee.label: Mariner Bay Medical Center, Transfer Center

transcript.speaker: RAC Desk
transcript.text: Mariner Bay transfer center? RAC hospital coordination desk. I need two minutes and straight answers.

transcript.speaker: RAC Desk
transcript.text: Ground and air transport to San Antonio and Victoria has stopped for good. I'm still holding the NICU and ICU beds we promised you. Did any patient actually leave overnight, who is still pending, and who is staying with you?

transcript.speaker: RAC Desk
transcript.text: Victoria Crossroads wants a clinical update on anyone they accepted. And if I don't have a firm count in thirty minutes, I release every bed you haven't claimed to the next hospital in line.

transcript.speaker: RAC Desk
transcript.text: Send the same numbers to your command center so everyone is working from one list. Stay safe over there.

voiceStyles.RAC Desk: Woman in her 40s, brisk and tired, a busy coordination desk behind her with phones ringing

snapshot.instructorNote: Core inject for the Transfer Center Liaison. Play the call and pause at each prompt for the liaison's answer. Watch whether the TCL reconciles the transferred and pending counts with the CNO before answering, tells the RAC which beds to keep or release (all of them if no patient left), offers clinical updates on anyone sent, and gives the same numbers to the command center and the PIO.
